subject: Keystone request: purge prompt/output/log artifacts + proof of removal
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@keystonehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Keystone Security <security@keystonehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request to purge prompt/response logs + proof of removal

Hi Soojin,

Keystone Health is requesting a full purge of prompt and assistant-output artifacts, related KV cache entries, and request/response logs for our production tenant (org: keystone-prod) in us-east-1. Scope attached (keystone_deletion_request_20250614.pdf) — it includes an authorized signatory and the set of resource identifiers (bucket prefixes, model endpoints, and job ids).

We need an audit-style proof of removal (hash manifest or CSV of removed object keys + timestamps) and confirmation of any retained audit metadata (we understand you keep a tamper-evident audit trail but Keystone needs to know what metadata remains and for how long). Can you confirm:
- Estimated ETA to complete the purge (target is within 5 business days)
- Which artifacts will be permanently removed vs. retained in sanitized form
- A link to the ops ticket where we can follow progress

Appreciate a short confirmation and an ops contact to follow up.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Head of Compliance, Keystone Health
priya@keystonehealth.com

Attachment: keystone_deletion_request_20250614.pdf (signed scope)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: Keystone Security <security@keystonehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to purge prompt/response logs + proof of removal

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear scope and the signed request. I’ve opened an ops ticket (REDW-3891) and looped in our on-call purge team. Ben (ops) and Marissa (privacy) will own execution and evidence delivery.

High-level answers up front:
- ETA: Target completion within 3 business days from ticket kickoff (we’ll confirm exact windows after we validate the resource list)
- Artifacts: We will remove prompt inputs, assistant outputs, prompt-derived KV entries, per-request logs and any transient traces. We retain tamper-evident audit entries (cryptographic hashes + minimal metadata) for 90 days by default; we can extend/shorten per contract — I’ll list exact fields you’ll see in the audit package.
- Ops ticket: https://redwood.app/ops/tickets/REDW-3891 (you should have view access; I’ve invited the Keystone Security group)

Ben/Marissa — next steps below. Priya, I’ll get you an ETA later today once Ben confirms scheduling with infra.

Thanks,
Soogin Lee
Senior Privacy & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Keystone request: purge prompt/response logs + proof of removal — ACTION: REDW-3891

Forwarding Keystone’s signed request (see attached). Summary of scope: keystone-prod, us-east-1 — remove: prompt inputs, model outputs, derived KV cache entries, per-request logs and any transient trace stores. Deliverable: CSV manifest of removed object keys + removal timestamps; MD5/SHA256 hashes for tamper-evidence; short ops runbook for audit (I attached a draft: ops_purge_runbook_20250615.md).

Checklist for this ticket (please reply with ETA and any blockers):
1) Validate resource list against infra (buckets, endpoint ids) — Connor
2) Schedule low-impact window to run sweep for the tenant — Ben
3) Generate proof manifest & sign hashes — Ben
4) Sanitize any retained audit metadata (minimize PII) and document retained fields — Marissa
5) Upload proof CSV to secure customer channel and notify Keystone Security — Soojin

Please keep the replies threaded and include the ticket ID in subject. This is high priority for Keystone’s regulatory timeline.

-- Soojin
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 19:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Keystone request: purge prompt/response logs + proof of removal — REDW-3891 COMPLETED

On Sat, 14 Jun 2025 15:25:00 -07:00 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Forwarding Keystone’s signed request (see attached).

Team — ticket REDW-3891 completed. Execution summary below (keystone-prod, us-east-1):

Steps executed:
- Validated resource list with Connor against infra mapping (buckets: s3://redwood-keystone-prod/requests/, endpoints: ep-kk-11, ep-kk-12).
- Ran targeted object deletion sweep for prefixes listed in the scope; removed 18,742 objects from S3 and 3 scheduled snapshots.
- Purged KV cache entries (region us-east-1) associated with tenant keyspace; invalidated LRU and deleted persisted cache files.
- Removed per-request logs from ephemeral logging pipeline (retention segment truncated and sealed).
- Rotated ephemeral ingestion keys used for those endpoints and invalidated session tokens created during the time window.
- Generated proof_of_sweep_20250617.csv containing removed object keys, deletion timestamps (UTC), and SHA256 hashes. The CSV is PGP-encrypted and uploaded to the secure customer bucket.

Retention note: as discussed, we keep a tamper-evident audit index (minimal metadata: sequence id, UTC timestamp, hash of removed object, and action code) for 90 days. No prompt or assistant content is retained in readable form. If Keystone requires zero-knowledge proof beyond hashes, we can schedule additional attestation steps.

Attachments: proof_of_sweep_20250617.csv (PGP-encrypted)
Ops ticket: https://redwood.app/ops/tickets/REDW-3891

ETA: work executed 2025-06-16 03:12:00 UTC — manifest generated and uploaded 2025-06-17 02:30:00 UTC.

Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proof_of_sweep_20250617.csv (PGP-encrypted manifest)
From: Priya Singh <priya@keystonehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Keystone Security <security@keystonehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KEYS: Purge confirmation and proof received — thanks

Hi Soojin / Ben —

Thanks for the quick execution and the detailed runbook. We received the PGP-encrypted manifest and have downloaded it to our secure folder. The SHA256 hashes match our internal ingest checks — that satisfies Keystone’s audit team for the scope provided.

A couple of small follow-ups:
- Can you confirm whether the 90-day audit index is a rolling retention (i.e., entries will expire automatically) or if it requires an ops request to remove earlier?
- Please send a short statement we can include in our internal DPIA record confirming that raw prompt/output content was removed and only cryptographic hashes + minimal metadata were kept.

If both are confirmed, Keystone will close the request on our side. Appreciate the transparency.

Best,
Priya Singh
Head of Compliance, Keystone Health

Attachment: none
